title: Baseline & launchpad
objective: Measure your honest starting line, set up every tool for the year, and write the PairCraft brief. No grinding yet.
theory: DSA problem protocol (restate → brute force → constraints → pattern → optimal → complexity → code → edge cases → alternative) and the mistake-log categories.
practice: 10 cold problems, Python install, first Python translation notes, account setup.
deliverables: learning-os repo with notes + mistake-log template
GitHub profile cleaned (3 pinned repos with READMEs)
Target list: Google entities + 8–10 parallel companies + 20 engineers
checkpoint: Python runs from a clean venv

knowledge: What is your diagnostic score and which pattern gaps did it expose?
What are the 9 steps of the problem protocol?
Name 5 JS→Python translations you wrote down
practical: Run hello.py from a fresh venv
Open the PairCraft brief and read it aloud in 2 minutes

tasks.text: Install Python 3.12+, uv or venv, VS Code Python extension. Create ~/dev/learning-os repo with notes/, dsa/, mistakes.md (columns: problem · gap type · re-solve dates 1d/7d/30d). Push it.
GitHub hygiene: profile photo, bio (“Full-stack engineer (MERN/TS) building LLM systems”), pin your 3 best repos, add a README to each (problem · stack · run · screenshot). Unpin tutorial clones.
Set the 5-hour daily block in your real calendar for 6 days/week: DSA · main block · light block · career. Add Day 7 as review/rest.
10-min recall: explain yesterday’s “Install Python 3.12+, uv or venv, VS Code Python extension” aloud without notes; write one gap you found.

Diagnostic: solve 10 LeetCode problems cold, untimed, in your current language (mix: 4 easy, 6 medium from Arrays/Hashing, Two Pointers, Trees). No videos. Log solved/unsolved + time per problem in mistakes.md. This is your baseline, not a test.

Read the 9-step problem protocol and the mistake-log categories (concept / pattern / implementation / complexity / communication). Write them at the top of mistakes.md; you will follow them on every problem from W2.
Create LeetCode + NeetCode accounts; open the NeetCode 150 roadmap and bookmark it. This list is the list — no list-hopping.
10-min recall: explain yesterday’s “Read the 9-step problem protocol and the mistake-log categories (concept / pattern / imple” aloud without notes; write one gap you found.
Accounts: AWS free tier with a $5 billing alert, Hugging Face, Kaggle, W&B, Render/Railway. Verify all 5 owned courses open in your Udemy library + 100xSchool schedule (note live-session days).
Tracking sheet (one tab): problems by pattern · mocks done · applications sent · referral conversations. Update weekly on Day 7, never daily.

Python first contact: read Official Tutorial ch. 1–3 as translation. Start notes/js-to-python.md: map/filter → comprehensions, npm/package.json → pip/venv/pyproject, async/await, const vs no-const, self, mutability.
10-min recall: explain yesterday’s “Accounts: AWS free tier with a $5 billing alert, Hugging Face, Kaggle, W&B, Render/Railway” aloud without notes; write one gap you found.

Target list in tracking sheet: Google entities to watch (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Gurugram; Munich if Germany stays a goal). Read 2 live Google SWE / AI-ML JDs and copy their minimum qualifications verbatim into notes/targets.md.

List 8–10 parallel companies (Amazon, Microsoft, Atlassian, Flipkart, Adobe, Razorpay, Swiggy, PhonePe, CRED, Meesho) and shortlist 20 engineers (mix SWE + applied AI) on LinkedIn for the Quiet Network. No messages yet.
Rewrite LinkedIn headline (“Full-Stack Engineer (MERN/TS) · building LLM & real-time systems · Python”) and About (500 chars: experience, what you build toward, 3 skills, 1 goal).
Create a venv, install requests + pytest, write hello.py that fetches a public JSON API and prints 3 fields. Run it from a clean terminal. Explain in js-to-python.md what differs from node_modules.
Attend/replay this week’s 100xSchool DSA + Web Dev sessions. Note only what is new to you.
10-min recall: explain yesterday’s “Create a venv, install requests + pytest, write hello.py that fetches a public JSON API an” aloud without notes; write one gap you found.

PairCraft requirements v0 (notes/paircraft/requirements.md): problem, users, MVP features, non-goals, success metrics (concurrent rooms, sync latency). Include: rooms, shared editor, voice/video, queued code runs, AI hints.

Read WebRTC overview (signaling, ICE/STUN/TURN, peer connection) and the Socket.IO rooms/adapter docs. Sketch the architecture on paper: client ↔ Socket.IO server ↔ Redis ↔ Postgres; WebRTC peer-to-peer media.

Weekly revision — Diagnostic, Dev environment, Tracking, GitHub hygiene: rewrite the key ideas from memory (no notes), then compare with your notes and fix the gaps. Reimplement two things from this week without looking.
Weekly review: answer this week’s knowledge questions aloud, run the practical checks, then write the three notes (struggled / learned / improve) in Weekly Plan → Review. Update the tracking sheet.
Plan next week: read W2’s objective and Day 1; move any unfinished 🔴 task into next week’s Day 1; confirm calendar blocks. Then rest — consistency beats intensity.
